description: Machine-readable expected outcome for every fixture in this directory. `verify-fixtures.mjs` reads this file and fails (non-zero exit) if any fixture's actual outcome does not match. This is a contract-first schema: it ships ahead of spec-lane's own estimator implementation, so every fixture here is a hand-authored example of a decision shape, not a captured real output. Fixture format version 2 (sol architect-review round) adds the required top-level `target` field to every fixture and the `predicted` field to every `status: "predicted"` fixture.
notes: sol architect-review must6: reason_codes is split into 11 BLOCKING codes and 1 ADVISORY code (DRIFT_WARNING). abstained requires >=1 BLOCKING code; predicted must carry NONE. See invalid-abstained-only-advisory and invalid-predicted-with-blocking-code.

prediction_interval.status=="available" is now exercised by predicted-with-available-interval (accept) in addition to the insufficient_data fixtures -- the M0-era note that v2 ships only insufficient_data no longer applies now that the "available" shape itself is frozen (schema if/then requires level/lower/upper/method/calibration_sample_size together); the calibration MATH that would compute real values in production is still M1 work, this fixture just proves the frozen shape validates.

fixtures.notes: Single BLOCKING reason_code (NOVEL_SURFACE_UNKNOWN): the surface has no comparable history at all, so applicability.status is "unknown" (not even out_of_domain -- there's no distance to measure against an empty population).
Two BLOCKING reason_codes together (INSUFFICIENT_POPULATION + DISTANCE_ABOVE_THRESHOLD): a small candidate population where the one eligible neighbor is still farther than distance_threshold.

MIXED_OR_UNATTRIBUTED_USAGE: every candidate in the population was excluded for this one reason (attribution/v1's fail-closed rule upstream means none of this population's usage is trustworthy input to a prediction).

status == "predicted" WITH reason_codes == ["DRIFT_WARNING"] (the one ADVISORY code) present at the same time -- demonstrates DRIFT_WARNING is advisory, not abstain-forcing and not itself a BLOCKING code: a point estimate still exists, flagged with a warning.
prediction_interval.status=="available" with all five fields present and lower<=upper -- exercises the frozen "available" shape (sol architect-review must6).
status == "abstained" but reason_codes == [] -- an unexplained abstain is indistinguishable from a silent failure, which v2 exists specifically to rule out.
reason_codes contains "STALE_CALIBRATION", not in the v2 closed set of 12 codes.

sol architect-review must6: status=="predicted" but reason_codes carries OUT_OF_DOMAIN, a BLOCKING code. A point estimate with a due-for-abstain reason attached is self-contradictory -- only the advisory DRIFT_WARNING may accompany a prediction.
sol architect-review must6: status=="abstained" with reason_codes==["DRIFT_WARNING"] -- the ONLY reason given is the advisory code, which does not by itself justify withholding a point estimate.

sol architect-review must6: prediction_interval.status=="available" but method/calibration_sample_size are missing -- the "available" shape is frozen in full (schema if/then), not left partially specified.
prediction_interval.lower (3.0) > upper (1.0) -- an inverted interval is meaningless regardless of how it was computed.
sol architect-review must7: population.eligible_count (9) exceeds population.candidate_count (5) -- eligible is always a subset of candidate, never larger.
sol architect-review must7: excluded_by_reason has a key ("TYPO_REASON") that is not one of the 12 reason_codes.
sol architect-review must7: excluded_by_reason.DISTANCE_ABOVE_THRESHOLD is -1, a negative count -- an excluded count can never be negative.

sol architect-review must7: a forbidden personal-dimension key ("reviewer") planted inside excluded_by_reason, an otherwise schema-unconstrained map. Also independently caught by excluded_by_reason_unknown_key ("reviewer" isn't a reason_code either) -- same defense-in-depth convention as agent-metrics/v1's own invalid-personal-dimension fixture. This fixture is specifically about proving the personal-dimension SCAN (newly added to estimate/v2 in this round) works, not just the reason-code closed-set check.
sol architect-review must7: routing_policy_digest carries a "sha256:" prefix, which the tightened pattern (^[0-9a-f]{64}$, bare hex only) no longer accepts.

sol architect-review 2nd round must B: decision.status=="abstained" but a top-level `predicted` object is present anyway. Schema-enforced via allOf/if-then-not (abstained forbids `predicted` from being present at all, not merely 'may be omitted') -- a point estimate alongside an admission that no prediction could be made is self-contradictory.

sol architect-review 2nd round must B: decision.status=="predicted" but applicability.status=="out_of_domain". Part of the tagged-union state machine: out_of_domain implies the decision must abstain -- there is no confident point estimate for a surface the population math says is out of domain. Schema-enforced via allOf/if-then-not.

sol architect-review 2nd round must B: prediction_interval.status=="insufficient_data" but level/lower/upper are present anyway. The "insufficient_data" branch is now closed to only `status` (schema if/then/else, the else side of the same conditional that freezes "available"'s full shape) -- these value fields are meaningless without enough calibration history to have computed them.

sol architect-review 2nd round must B: prediction_interval.level is 1.5 -- a confidence level is a fraction, exclusively between 0 and 1 (exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum; 0 and 1 themselves are also degenerate and excluded, not just values above 1).

sol architect-review 2nd round must B, main裁定 (exclusive primary-reason counting): candidate_count=42, eligible_count=38 (a gap of 4 excluded candidates), but excluded_by_reason=={} (sum 0). Every excluded candidate must be counted under exactly one reason -- an empty map claiming zero candidates needed a reason, when 4 were in fact excluded, silently drops the accounting.

sol architect-review 3rd round must2: decision.status=="abstained" but prediction_interval.status=="available" (fully shaped). An available confidence interval is an interval AROUND a point estimate; an abstained decision has no point estimate, so the two cannot coexist. Schema-enforced via allOf/if-then (prediction_interval.status=="available" forces decision.status=="predicted").

sol architect-review 3rd round must2: prediction_interval.calibration_sample_size is 0 -- a leave-one-out calibration computed from zero samples is not a calibration, it's the absence of one (already representable as status=="insufficient_data"). Minimum raised from 0 to 1.
